title: Automatic Config Healer with Proposal Simulations and Cost Safety
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build an "automatic config healer" service that proposes safe configuration changes (batching, cache TTLs, kernel hints) via a simulation sandbox, applies staged proposals using traffic slices and shadow applies, and automatically reconciles or rolls back live state when regressions are detected. The goal is to reduce per-token cost by surfacing high-confidence batching/caching recommendations while ensuring no user-facing SLO regressions and bounded economic risk.
acceptance_criteria: Simulation sandbox can run a proposed config against a representative request trace and produce deterministic cost/latency delta estimates within ±10% of live behavior
Proposal objects include provenance, risk score, and an apply-stepping plan (shadow -> canary -> ramp)
Automated rollback triggers if latency P95 or error rate exceed configured hysteresis thresholds within the canary window
State reconciliation can detect drift between desired config and live state and either repair (idempotent apply) or surface manual rollback candidates
Telemetry for each proposal shows token-level cost, batching efficiency (batch size distribution), KV cache hit-rate, and a rollback likelihood score
technical_notes: Simulation harness will reuse the existing replay store (s3://replays/representative-traces) with sampling control to match production seq-len distribution
Proposal model: {desired_config, prev_config, diffs, provenance, expected_cost_delta, expected_latency_delta, risk_score, apply_plan}
Apply plan consists of: dry-shadow apply (no traffic), canary (1% slice), adaptive ramp with economic stop-loss, and stabilized global apply
Rollback triggers: composite rule combining SLO breach (latency/error), cost overshoot threshold, and heuristic detection of batching inversion (larger batches causing queueing)
Reconciliation approach: three-way snapshot merge (live, desired, last-known-good) with safe patching by generating idempotent operations and tombstones for removed keys
State storage: store stable snapshots per change in config-store with cryptographic provenance (commit id + signature) to enable deterministic rewinds
We will expose a 'proposal sandbox' API for PM/Design to preview UI changes and for SRE to run manual fault-injection scenarios
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Build simulation harness and replay connector (internal only)
Phase 1: Implement proposal object, risk scoring, and UI preview endpoint
Phase 2: Shadow apply plumbing + telemetry collection on a small subset of models
Phase 3: Canary traffic slice with automated monitoring and rollback automation enabled (opt-in teams)
Phase 4: Gradual ramp and enable reconciliation automation for non-critical routes
Phase 5: Full rollout with audit logs, manual-override, and postmortem playbooks
comments: 2026-03-01 - Asha Patel: Created ticket. Initial spike showed simulation cost deltas correlate well for short-sequence traces but diverge for >1024 token flows. Need better long-seq sampling.
2026-03-03 - Liam Chen: Prototype of replay connector merged in feature branch; added sequence-length weighting and user-segmentation so we don't bias towards small interactive requests.

2026-03-05 - SRE (review): Concern about automatic global roll-forward if reconciliation incorrectly repairs an intermediate state. Suggested adding a 'safety budget' per tenant that limits economic exposure and requires manual approval above threshold.

2026-03-07 - Data Science (review): Proposed risk_score model: weighted features = [expected_latency_delta, expected_cost_delta, cache_hit_delta, batch_size_change, historical-stability-score]. Will supply a baseline model for POC.

2026-03-09 - Liam Chen: Implemented basic rollback trigger prototype: monitors P95, error-rate, and cost-per-token. Added hysteresis window and noise-filtering. Next: integrate with reconciliation module to attempt safe repair before rolling back.
2026-03-10 - PM (Marta Kovacs): Prioritize opt-in teams and documentation. Add checklist for compliance-sensitive tenants (ensuring KMS/keys unaffected by automated applies).
